items.q: Which of the following is an example of value that a service provider's EMPLOYEES may receive?
o: Dividends paid on shares
Taxes paid to the government
Lower prices for consumers
Career and professional development and a sense of purpose
items.x: Different stakeholders receive different value. Employees may gain financial and non-financial incentives, development and purpose. Dividends go to shareholders and taxes benefit society.

items.q: What is a service relationship?
o: A contract between two suppliers
A cooperation between a service provider and a service consumer, which includes service provision, service consumption and service relationship management
A document describing the services offered to a consumer group
The reporting line between a service owner and a manager
items.x: A service relationship is a cooperation between provider and consumer. It includes service provision, service consumption and service relationship management.

items.q: Which statement about products is CORRECT?
o: Products are typically complex and not fully visible to the consumer, and one product can be the basis of several service offerings
A product is always a physical item
Consumers can always see all of the resources that make up a product
Each product can only be offered to one consumer group
items.x: A product is a configuration of an organization's resources, many of which the consumer never sees. The same product can be packaged into different service offerings for different consumer groups.

items.q: A hospital outsources its payroll to a specialist provider. Which is a cost REMOVED from the hospital by this service?
o: The fee paid to the payroll provider
The effort to integrate HR data with the provider's system
Maintaining the hospital's own payroll software and the staff to run it
Training HR staff on the provider's portal
items.x: Maintaining its own payroll system and staff is a cost the service removes. The fee, the integration effort and the training are costs imposed on the consumer.

items.q: A company uses a managed backup service. Which risk does the service REMOVE from the company?
o: Dependency on the backup provider's financial stability
A breach of the provider's security controls
The provider failing to meet its contract
Losing data because the company's own backup tapes fail
items.x: The service takes over the risk of the company's own backups failing. Dependency on the provider, provider breaches and contract failures are risks imposed by using the service.

items.q: Which statement about utility and warranty is CORRECT?
o: Both utility and warranty are needed for a product or service to facilitate the desired outcomes and create value
Utility is more important than warranty in all cases
Warranty describes the features of a service
A service with good utility does not need warranty
items.x: Utility is what the product or service does, and warranty is how well it performs, covering availability, capacity, security and continuity. A feature-rich service that is often unavailable does not create value, and neither does a reliable service that does not meet the need.

items.q:
A hospital introduces a new appointment system. Which two of the following are OUTCOMES?
1. Appointment confirmation emails are sent automatically
2. Patients wait fewer days to see a doctor
3. Clinic managers can plan staffing more accurately
4. A new database server is installed
o: 1 and 2
1 and 4
2 and 3
3 and 4
items.x: Outcomes are results for stakeholders: shorter waiting times for patients and better planning for managers. Sending emails and installing a server are outputs, meaning deliverables of activities.

items.q: What is a service level agreement (SLA)?
o: An internal agreement between two teams of the same provider
A documented agreement between a service provider and a customer that identifies both the services required and the expected level of service
A contract between a provider and its hardware supplier
A list of all products in the portfolio
items.x: An SLA is agreed with the customer and describes the services and expected service levels. Good SLAs relate to outcomes and experience, not only to operational metrics.

items.q: What is a configuration item (CI)?
o: Any component that needs to be managed in order to deliver an IT service
Any financially valuable component
Any change of state that is significant
A request for a new feature
items.x: A CI is any component that needs to be managed to deliver an IT service, such as servers, applications, documentation and even services. Option B describes an IT asset.

items.q: What is an IT asset?
o: Any component that needs to be managed to deliver a service
A record of a change
A version of a service made available for use
Any financially valuable component that can contribute to the delivery of an IT product or service
items.x: An IT asset is any financially valuable component that can contribute to the delivery of an IT product or service. IT asset management manages assets across their whole lifecycle, from acquisition to disposal.

items.q:
Identify the missing word in the following sentence.
A [?] is a version of a service or other configuration item, or a collection of configuration items, that is made available for use.
o: change
release
deployment
baseline
items.x: A release is a version of a service or CI, or a collection of CIs, that is made available for use. Deployment moves components into an environment, and that can happen separately from the release.

items.q: Which statement about experience in ITIL is CORRECT?
o: Experience matters only for external customers, not for employees
Experience is fully captured by system uptime figures
Experience is an important part of how users and customers perceive value, and should be understood through their feedback, not only through technical metrics
Experience is the responsibility of the service desk alone
items.x: Experience, covering both the functional and emotional aspects of interactions, strongly shapes perceived value and quality. It applies to customers, users and employees, and is understood through feedback and experience measures as well as technical data.

items.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the four dimensions of product and service management?
o: Organizations and people
Governance and compliance
Partners and suppliers
Value streams and processes
items.x: The four dimensions are organizations and people, information and technology, partners and suppliers, and value streams and processes. Governance is a component of the value system, not a dimension.

items.q: A retailer works with a specialist analytics firm because it would take the retailer years to build the same expertise. Which factor influencing supplier strategy is this?
o: Demand patterns
Corporate culture
External constraints
Subject matter expertise
items.x: Using a supplier for expertise the organization does not have, and cannot quickly build, illustrates subject matter expertise as a factor in supplier strategy.

items.q: Users increasingly expect to use services from their phones, at any time and from any place. Under PESTLE, which type of external factor is this?
o: Social
Legal
Political
Economic
items.x: Changing expectations, behaviours and working patterns of people, such as hybrid working and mobile access, are Social factors.

items.q: When selecting a new monitoring tool, a team checks that it integrates with the existing architecture and that storing data in the vendor's region complies with regulations. Which dimension are these considerations MAINLY part of?
o: Organizations and people
Value streams and processes
Information and technology
Partners and suppliers
items.x: Technology choices in the information and technology dimension consider compatibility with the existing architecture, regulatory compliance for information, security, and the long-term viability of the technology.

items.q: Compared with the ITIL 4 value chain, which ITIL (Version 5) lifecycle activities cover the work that ITIL 4 grouped under 'deliver and support'?
o: Operate, Deliver and Support
Discover and Design
Acquire and Build
Design and Transition
items.x: Version 5 separates running the live product (Operate), making it available and usable for consumers (Deliver), and helping users and restoring service (Support). ITIL 4 grouped these under 'deliver and support'.

items.q: A company contracts specialist engineers and signs an agreement with a cloud provider, because both are needed before a new product can be built. Which lifecycle activity is this?
o: Discover
Transition
Acquire
Operate
items.x: Acquire obtains the components needed to create and deliver products and services, including technology, supplier services and people, through buying, building or partnering.

items.q: Which lifecycle activity helps users with issues, restores normal operation when something goes wrong, and feeds what is learned back into Discover and Design?
o: Build
Acquire
Transition
Support
items.x: Support assists users and restores normal operation. Its insights should flow back into Discover and Design to improve the product, which is one reason the lifecycle is non-linear.

items.q: How are the product and service lifecycle activities typically used in practice?
o: They are performed once each, in strict order, for every product
They are combined into value streams designed for specific scenarios, supported by management practices
They are performed only by the IT department
They replace the need for management practices
items.x: Organizations combine lifecycle activities into value streams, for example 'restore a failed service' or 'launch a new feature'. Practices provide the resources and capabilities used within those activities.

items.q: Operations staff are reminded that even routine work, such as handling user requests, should be done with the consumer's desired outcomes in mind. Which recommendation of 'focus on value' does this reflect?
o: Include a focus on value in every step of improvement initiatives
Know who the service provider is
Focus on value during normal operational activity as well as during improvement initiatives
Measure value only through cost
items.x: Value should guide day-to-day operations, not only improvement projects. Every staff member's work should link to value for consumers and other stakeholders.

items.q: A team finds that the network group already runs an effective peer-review process for changes, and extends it to other teams instead of designing a new one. Which guiding principle does this illustrate?
o: Start where you are
Optimize and automate
Think and work holistically
Keep it simple and practical
items.x: When good practices are found in existing services or methods that can be replicated or expanded, 'start where you are' recommends using them instead of starting from scratch.

items.q: In the context of 'progress iteratively with feedback', what is a feedback loop?
o: A meeting held once at the end of a project
A survey sent to all customers each year
A cycle of approvals for every change
A situation in which part of the output of an activity is used as new input
items.x: A feedback loop uses part of an activity's output as new input, so the work can be adjusted continuously. Feedback is sought before, during and after each iteration.

items.q: A team explains a planned change to executives using business impact, and to engineers using technical detail. Which guidance from 'collaborate and promote visibility' does this follow?
o: Collaboration does not mean consensus
Communicate in a way the audience can hear
Recognize the complexity of the system
Simplify before automating
items.x: Different audiences need different messages and levels of detail. Choosing the right method and message for each audience improves understanding and engagement.

items.q: 'Where possible, look for patterns in the needs of and interactions between system elements' is guidance for applying which guiding principle?
o: Focus on value
Start where you are
Think and work holistically
Collaborate and promote visibility
items.x: Working holistically involves understanding how system elements interact. Patterns help predict needs and design coordinated solutions.

items.q: Which statement is a recommendation for applying 'keep it simple and practical'?
o: Analyse every detail before acting
Automate first and simplify later
Involve every stakeholder in every decision
Simplicity is the best route to achieving quick wins
items.x: Recommendations include: ensure value, simplicity is the ultimate sophistication, do fewer things but do them better, respect people's time, easier to understand means more likely to adopt, and simplicity is the best route to quick wins.

items.q: According to 'optimize and automate', what does optimization mean?
o: Making something as effective and useful as it needs to be
Making something perfect before it is released
Replacing people with technology
Reducing the cost of a process to zero
items.x: Optimization means making something as effective and useful as it needs to be, not perfect. It should happen before automation and be measured with agreed metrics.

items.q: Which governance activity involves assessing the organization, its strategy, portfolios and relationships with other parties, as stakeholder needs and circumstances change?
o: Direct
Evaluate
Monitor
Improve
items.x: 'Evaluate' looks at the organization and its environment so that the governing body can then direct, through strategy and policy, and monitor performance and conformance.

items.q: Which statement about governance within the ITIL value system is CORRECT?
o: Governance applies only to financial reporting
Management practices operate independently of governance
Governance is performed by the service desk
Lifecycle activities and management practices should be aligned with the direction set by the governing body
items.x: The governing body sets direction through strategy and policy. Practices and activities must align with that direction, and governance itself should also be continually improved.

items.q: Which is the correct order of the first four steps of the continual improvement model?
o: Where are we now? > What is the vision? > How do we get there? > Where do we want to be?
Take action > What is the vision? > Where are we now? > Did we get there?
What is the vision? > Where are we now? > Where do we want to be? > How do we get there?
Where do we want to be? > Where are we now? > Take action > What is the vision?
items.x: The model runs: What is the vision? Where are we now? Where do we want to be? How do we get there? Take action. Did we get there? How do we keep the momentum going?

items.q: What happens in the 'Take action' step of the continual improvement model?
o: The improvement plan is executed, often iteratively, while risks are managed and the team stays open to changes
The vision and mission are defined
The baseline assessment is carried out
Successes are celebrated and lessons recorded
items.x: 'Take action' carries out the plan. This can be done in iterations, as a project, or with Agile methods, while monitoring progress and adjusting as needed.

items.q: How should continual improvement be reflected in agreements with suppliers and partners?
o: Suppliers should be excluded from improvement activities
Contracts should include requirements for measurement, reporting and improvement
Suppliers should only be measured on price
Improvement should be handled only at contract renewal
items.x: Suppliers and partners contribute to value, so their contracts should include measurement, reporting and continual improvement obligations.

items.q: Which statement about management practices is CORRECT?
o: A practice is the same as a single process
Practices are owned by one department and used by one value chain activity
A practice includes resources from all four dimensions, such as people, information, technology, suppliers and processes
Practices are only relevant to IT teams
items.x: A practice is a set of organizational resources for performing work or accomplishing an objective. It includes people, information and technology, partners and suppliers, and value streams and processes. A process is only one element of a practice.

items.q: What is the purpose of the service desk practice?
o: To restore normal service as quickly as possible
To set clear business-based targets for service levels
To protect the information needed by the organization
To capture demand for incident resolution and service requests, and to be the entry point and single point of contact for the service provider with all of its users
items.x: The service desk is the single point of contact for users. It captures demand for incident resolution and service requests and shapes much of the user experience.

items.q: In the ITIL value system, what is 'demand'?
o: The need or desire for products and services among internal and external consumers
Options to improve the organization
The output of the value system
A request from management to reduce costs
items.x: Demand is the need or desire for products and services among internal and external consumers. With opportunity, it is an input that triggers activities in the value system.

items.q: Which statement about the ITIL value system is CORRECT?
o: It is a strict sequence of steps that must be followed in order
It describes how its components and activities work together flexibly to turn opportunity and demand into value
It applies only to external service providers
It replaces the need for governance
items.x: The value system is a flexible system. Guiding principles, governance, lifecycle and value chain activities, practices and continual improvement work together to enable value creation.

items.q: What is the main difference between a value stream and a process?
o: A process always crosses several organizations, while a value stream stays within one team
There is no difference
A value stream is a type of software
A value stream is an end-to-end series of steps from demand to value for a consumer, while a process is a set of activities that transforms inputs into outputs, often within one practice
items.x: Value streams show the consumer's end-to-end journey and often cross teams and practices. Processes make individual steps consistent and controlled. Both matter, and processes should be optimized in the context of the value streams they serve.

items.q: A value stream deals with a new type of problem where cause and effect only become clear afterwards. Which approach is MOST appropriate?
o: Follow a rigid, fully documented procedure
Wait until a perfect solution is designed
Experiment with small, safe-to-fail actions, observe the results and adapt
Outsource the value stream immediately
items.x: In complex contexts, outcomes are hard to predict, so experimentation and feedback work better than fixed procedures. Ordered contexts, where cause and effect are known, suit standard procedures and good practice.

items.q: Which list shows the six capabilities of the ITIL AI Capability Model?
o: Plan, Build, Run, Monitor, Improve, Retire
Creation, Curation, Clarification, Cognition, Communication, Coordination
Discover, Design, Acquire, Build, Transition, Operate
Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability, Authentication, Authorization, Accounting
items.x: The AI Capability Model, sometimes called the 6C model, describes six AI capabilities: creation, curation, clarification, cognition, communication and coordination. It helps organizations understand and govern their use of AI.

items.q: Which statement BEST describes the relationship between ITIL and ISO/IEC 20000-1?
o: ISO/IEC 20000-1 specifies requirements for a service management system against which organizations can be certified, and ITIL guidance can help organizations meet those requirements
ITIL is the certification standard for organizations, and ISO/IEC 20000-1 is training guidance
ISO/IEC 20000-1 requires all organizations to use ITIL
They cover completely unrelated topics
items.x: ISO/IEC 20000-1 states what a service management system must achieve and can be audited and certified. ITIL describes how good service management can be achieved, so it helps organizations meet the standard without being required by it.
